module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 15

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15)
- [BJP14] T. Brown, V. Jungić and A. Poelstra, "On double 3-term arithmetic progressions",
  Integers 14 (2014), Paper No. A43.
- [CCS14] J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, "Avoidance of additive cubes and
  related results", Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace Green15

/--
Does there exist a Lipschitz function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose graph
$\Gamma = \{(n, f(n)) : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ is free of 3-term progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 3 := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [BJP14].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15_ap4 :
    ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree  {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 4 := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add finitary version

end Green15

findings.description: The module bibliography's [CCS14] entry (lines 27–28) has the wrong title and publication details: it lists “Avoidance of additive cubes and related results”, Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66. The relevant Cassaigne–Currie–Schaeffer–Shallit paper is “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, published in J. ACM. This is a reference error only; both Lean statements remain mathematically faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Green's bibliography, reference [65], gives “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum. J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Art. 10, 17 pp.” (https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf). Shallit's 2014 publication list independently gives the same title and publication (https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~shallit/papers.html#2014). The paper's LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1106.5204 confirms the title and proves the additive-cube avoidance result used here.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [CCS14] bibliography entry with: J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Article 10, 17 pp. Optionally link https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.5204.

sources_consulted: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15 — Problem 15, its comments, and references [58] and [65]; current document records its latest update as December 2025.
https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/o43/o43.pdf — Brown, Jungić and Poelstra, “On double 3-term arithmetic progressions”, particularly the introduction and the 4-term consequence on page 3.
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~shallit/papers.html — 2014 publication entry and link to the 2011 preprint.
https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.5204 — title, authors, abstract and version history.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/1106.5204 — LaTeX source, including additive-power definitions, the explicit morphism, the additive-cube avoidance theorem, and the open-problems section.
Local checkout: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/AP/Basic.lean; Mathlib's Lipschitz definitions, Nat/Int metric instances, and ENat.card definition; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in Green15.green_15 or Green15.green_15_ap4. Green's current source agrees with their open/solved tags. The [BJP14] citation for the 4-term variant is valid: that paper explicitly states the consequence on page 3. Scratch Lean checks compiled successfully and verified the usual metric interpretation, nontrivial progression semantics, graph infinitude, and that K = 0 cannot provide a witness. A finite test of the CCS morphism also behaved as expected. The related Erdős 193 webpage was Cloudflare-blocked; the accessible sources suffice to verify both declarations. The reviewed file was not modified.
